_docs.purpose: Single source of truth for the CLI-visible knob surface: every config key, dotted config path, CLI flag, embedder (engine request) field, and external-tool flag that a zzop message is allowed to name. Consumed by crates/config (the Rust config front-end's unknown-key drift warnings) AND by crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/'s reference-validation meta-test (CHECK A / CHECK B), so both sides of the contract read the exact same data — a config key or flag can never drift between what the config front-end accepts and what the engine's own rule/warning messages are allowed to recommend. RECOGNIZED IS WIRED (2026-07-26): every key listed here is either forwarded into the engine request or drives this front-end's own mapping. It was not always so — `failOn`, `format` and `report.*` (dir/formats/enabled) sat here for months as vocabulary with no consumer, accepted and forwarded nowhere once the JS CLI that read them was removed (2026-07-20). That is a silent failure, not a harmless listing: an author who wrote `failOn` got no warning, no error, and no gate. All three were RETIRED from this file on 2026-07-26, so they now fall through to the unknown-key walk — which names them as REMOVED rather than as typos (`crates/config/src/mapper/warnings.rs`'s `RETIRED_KEYS`). A shipped message may no longer name them. Restoring one is a few lines if a consuming surface is ever built; until then, absence is the honest state. NOTE on the empty `configKeys.report`: the scope key survives with a zero-length list ONLY because `crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/config_surface.rs`'s `ConfigKeysSurface` still declares `report` as a required serde field — deleting the key here breaks that deserialization. Delete the two together.
_docs.configKeys: The fixed-shape config object's known keys, by scope (originally the removed JS mapper's KNOWN_KEYS constant; now the Rust config front-end's). See crates/config's own doc for the 'warn on drift, never reject' contract this backs. Path resolution bases: `trees[].root` is resolved to absolute against a caller-supplied `base_dir` by the config front-end (crates/config), see crates/config/src/mapper/paths.rs's doc comment; `overlays` entries (both top-level and `trees[].overlays`) are instead resolved by both dialects against the OWNING TREE's own root, never `base_dir`. For the zzop-mcp server specifically (verified against crates/config/src/trees.rs + crates/config/src/paths.rs + crates/config/src/lib.rs): `base_dir` is NOT a fixed value — it is either the tool call's own (already-absolutized) tree root (`analyze_repo`, and `cross_repo`'s config-free `paths` mode), or the directory containing the (already-absolutized) `configPath` (`cross_repo`'s config-first mode). The absolutizing step itself is the actionable part: a RELATIVE `path`/`paths`/`configPath` tool argument is resolved by the MCP HOST PROCESS against ITS OWN current working directory (`std::path::absolute`, i.e. wherever the client happened to launch/configure the `zzop-mcp mcp` process) — a directory the calling MCP client cannot see or rely on. Consequently: always pass ABSOLUTE paths for the `path`/`paths`/`configPath` tool arguments in MCP usage, and prefer an absolute `trees[].root` when authoring a `zzop.config.jsonc` consumed via `configPath`, so no part of the join depends on the server process's unseen cwd. `packs.extraDirs` is the config-file dialect for adding a DSL rule-pack directory — do not write `packsDir` in a `zzop.config.jsonc` (that's the embedder request field a host application sets directly; see `embedderFieldShapes.packsDir` for its own back-reference). DEFAULT DISCOVERY (2026-07-26): when `packs.extraDirs` is not declared AT ALL, the front end falls back to exactly one location — `zzop/rules/` under the resolution base (`crates/config`'s `DEFAULT_AUTHORED_PACKS_DIR`) — and only when that directory actually exists. A declared `extraDirs` always wins outright, the empty array included (that is the explicit opt-out); the two are never merged, so there is exactly one source of truth for where packs came from. A missing `zzop/rules/` is silence, not a warning. This is the user-authored half of the on-disk two-way split: `.zzop/` is tool-derived and disposable, `zzop/` is authored and belongs in version control.
_docs.vocabulary: CONVENTION VOCABULARY — the names a PROJECT picks, declared instead of guessed. A name vocabulary splits three ways: a FACT is fixed by a framework or a language (`@GetMapping`, `router.post`) and stays built in because nobody can rename it; a CAP/THRESHOLD is a number, not a name, and is out of scope (`rules.<id>` option overrides remain unsupported); a CONVENTION is a name the project itself chooses — what it calls its auth guards, which URL segments mark its API, where its Java sources live, which directories hold build output. Holding a convention as a built-in literal means the engine GUESSES what a project calls its own things and silently misclassifies every project that names them differently, which is the failure `git.commitSubjectPatterns` already refuses on the commit-subject axis. Owner of the values: `zzop_engine::VocabularyConfig::built_in()`, which references the constant each consuming rule/pass already owned — this front end does NOT read those symbols to inject anything — nothing is injected (see below). They are the values `zzop init` writes into the starter file, so the only way a built-in reaches a run is that the author's config states it. MERGE POLICY, per key, whole replacement: a key the author names replaces its built-in list/pattern OUTRIGHT — never an element-wise merge, the same one-origin rule `packs.extraDirs` and `git.commitTypePatterns` state, because a merged vocabulary has two authors and neither can say what the effective set is. THE KEY IS THE LEAF, not the branch it hangs under (spelled out 2026-07-27, when `vocabulary.featureSlicedDesign` became the first nested scope here): declaring `featureSlicedDesign.entry` replaces the entry list and leaves `featureSlicedDesign.shared`/`featureSlicedDesign.sliceContainers`/`featureSlicedDesign.baseDirs` exactly as they were, the same way `packs.disabled` does not clear `packs.extraDirs` and `git.since` does not clear `git.recentDays`. Every nested scope in this config has always worked that way; it went unwritten only because `vocabulary` was flat until now, and the omission cost a wrong design conclusion the first time someone reasoned about it — branch-level replacement would combine with the rule that an undeclared key makes no judgment, to mean a one-line edit silently switches three sibling judgments off, which is precisely why the leaf rule is the one in force. A key the author does not name IS NOT JUDGED, and a declared-but-EMPTY value (`null`, `""`, `[]`) means the same thing — there is no built-in fallback arm left (removed 2026-07-27). The built-in values still exist, but only as the defaults `zzop init` writes into the starter config, so they reach a run because the config SAYS them, never behind the author. Note the direction this costs in: an undeclared exemption vocabulary grants no exemption and an undeclared guard vocabulary proves no guard, so leaving a key out makes rules fire MORE, not less. Measured 2026-07-29 across a 17-repo corpus, declaring the shipped template vocabulary took `mutating-route-no-auth` from 58 findings to 6 — an unconfigured project is a noisy project, deliberately, because under-clearing is recoverable and over-clearing is silent. That is also why 'declare nothing' must never be spellable as 'treat everything as a guard': an empty guard PATTERN would be a regex matching every name. Turning a judgment off is what `rules: { "<id>": "off" }` is for. A declared pattern that does not compile as a regex matches nothing (never a panic). WHY `git.commitTypePatterns`/`git.commitSubjectPatterns` ARE NOT UNDER THIS ROOF, though they are the same KIND of thing: `git.*` configures the git COLLECTOR and those two tables are matched against commit MESSAGES — prose a human wrote, not an identifier in the analyzed source. Every key here instead names something the code itself spells. Different subject matter, different roof; and they are shipped keys besides, so moving them would break configs for no gain. Do not 'unify' the two blocks. CACHE: a declared vocabulary changes what a run EXTRACTS, not only what it reports — the ORM-receiver pattern decides which write sites a file has, the Prisma client getter decides which db-table consumes exist, the router-mount guard words decide a fragment's auth-guarded attribute, and moneyTokens decides a cached Prisma finding. So the WHOLE vocabulary object is hashed into both halves of every cache key (`zzop_engine::cache::vocabulary_fingerprint`, present in `IrKey` as well as `CacheKey`): editing any key here misses the warm entries written under the previous one rather than being served their answers. Deliberately the whole object rather than the per-lane subset — a subset is a hand-maintained claim about which lane reads what, and over-invalidating costs a recompute while under-invalidating serves a WRONG answer. `vocabulary.skipDirs` lands on `DispatchConfig::skip_dirs` (the walker's skip list, which already owned it) rather than on the engine's vocabulary struct, so one list has one owner. `vocabulary.workspaceSkipDirs` is consumed by this FRONT END alone (`trees: "auto"` workspace discovery, crates/config/src/workspaces.rs) and is deliberately NOT forwarded into the request — a forwarded key no engine surface reads is the 'recognized but wired nowhere' defect `RETIRED_KEYS` had to clean up.
_docs.rulesValues: A `rules.<ruleId>` entry (see crates/config/src/mapper/options.rs — the Rust config front end accepts EXACTLY two shapes and rejects everything else) is either of exactly two shapes: (1) a severity/disable STRING token, or (2) an OBJECT `{ severity, exclude }` (the `ruleObject` shape above) whose `severity` key (optional) takes the same string token and whose `exclude` key (optional) is an array of path substrings/globs. The string form maps through `SEVERITY_ALIASES`: `critical`/`error`/`err`/`high` -> critical, `warning`/`warn`/`medium` -> warning, `info`/`information`/`note`/`low` -> info, and `off`/`none`/`disable`/`disabled` disables the rule entirely — `"off"` (or any of its aliases) is how a rule is disabled via config, as opposed to the embedder dialect's `disabledRules` list (camelCase is the ONLY wire spelling — the request surfaces serialize with `rename_all = "camelCase"` and no alias, so a snake_case `disabled_rules` key in a JSON request is silently dropped, never an error). ANY other value shape — a bare boolean (`false` included — there is no boolean dialect; writing `"ruleId": false` to disable a rule is invalid, use `"off"`), a number, an array, `null`, or an object without `severity`/`exclude` — is rejected with a load-time `ConfigError` naming the rule id (`rules.<ruleId> must be a severity string (e.g. "warn"/"off") or an object ({ "severity": ..., "exclude": [...] }).`), never silently ignored and never treated as disabling the rule.
_docs.configPaths: Every valid DOTTED spelling of a nested config key, in the form an author would actually write it in a message: `<parent>.<child>` for a fixed-shape nested object (e.g. `git.since`), `<parent>[].<child>` for a per-entry field of an array-of-objects (e.g. `trees[].root`), nesting through both when the scope itself is nested (e.g. `trees[].topology.mounts[].dir`). DERIVED FROM configKeys, AND ENFORCED AS SUCH: crates/config's `config_paths_are_derived_from_config_keys` test regenerates this whole list from configKeys — one declared dotted prefix per scope, an unknown scope failing the test — and compares it to what is written here, so a nested key can no longer be present in configKeys and silently absent here. That was not hypothetical: `mount`/`route` were listed in configKeys with ZERO dotted entries here while this line already claimed derivation, and nothing detected it (a false negative, i.e. real dotted paths that a shipped message could not legally name). Exactly two scopes are deliberately not dotted, and the test names both: `top` (a top-level key IS its own spelling — the configKeys.top list, never a dotted path) and `ruleObject` (`rules.<id>.severity`/`rules.<id>.exclude` — `<id>` is an open-keyed rule id, not enumerable here; a message naming a specific rule id under `rules` is checked as a JSON-snippet shape instead, see the rule_contracts meta-test's CHECK B doc).
_docs.cliFlags: The flags the `zzop` binary recognizes (packages/cli-bin/src/main.rs + its cli/ argv helpers): `--config` (the config-first modifier every multi-tree subcommand takes — `cross`/`endpoint`/`manifest`/`facts`/`graph` — AND, since 2026-07-27, the single-tree `analyze`: a config that does not sit at the tree root was otherwise unreachable from a terminal, so the old 'the fixed-arity analyze is deliberately not one of them' note is retired), `--allow-tool-drift` (the `diff` modifier that downgrades the cross-build REFUSAL to a disclosed comparison — see docs/modules/facade.md's manifest/diff section), `--scope <prefix>`, `--top <n>`, `--fold <n>`, `--domain <join|dep|risk|posture|cochange>` and `--format <mermaid|cosmograph-nodes|cosmograph-links>` (the `graph` modifiers: `--scope` keeps only rows whose source id or a site path starts with the prefix, `--top` caps rows PER BUCKET — both optional, both disclosed inside the emitted mermaid document whether they fire or not; `--domain` picks WHICH RELATION connects two nodes and `--fold <n>` picks WHAT A NODE IS, drawing each path's first n segments as one box. `--fold` is accepted only by the domains whose nodes are paths (`dep`/`cochange`, owned by `GraphDomain::accepts_fold`) and REFUSED by `risk`/`posture`/`join`, whose nodes are engine verdicts and io keys — the same no-knob-that-does-nothing rule `--top` follows on the cosmograph lane. A fold depth of 0 is an argument-shape error, and a folded edge is labelled with the number of file-level edges it collapsed; `--format` picks how the result is serialized. `--format cosmograph-*` is accepted only with `--domain dep` and REFUSES `--top` rather than ignoring it — that lane is deliberately uncapped for an interactive viewer, and a silently-ignored flag is the exact defect class this whitelist exists to catch; its census goes to stderr so stdout stays a parseable NDJSON table), `--source-id <id>` (the `file` modifier that picks WHICH tree answers when several declare the same relative path — added 2026-07-28 to close a host-parity hole: the shared `file_summary` had always taken it and the `check_file` MCP tool had always passed it, while this binary passed none, so the CLI reply could name other candidate trees in `otherTrees` and give its own caller no way to ask about them), `--severity <critical|warning|info>`, `--rule <id>` and `--limit <n>` (the findings-view knobs on the three analysis lanes `analyze`/`analyze-envelope`/`cross` — the argv spelling of the identically-named MCP tool arguments, parsed into the one shared `FindingFilters`, so neither surface can filter differently), `--force` (the `init` modifier, and the ONLY argument that subcommand takes: without it an existing config file is left alone and the run refuses rather than overwrite it), `--verbose` (the `version` modifier on BOTH binaries — `zzop version --verbose` / `zzop-mcp version --verbose` add every parser's fingerprint to the bare release version), `--version`, and `--help`/`-h`, `--version`/`-V` (accepted after any subcommand too, printing that subcommand's own line to stdout with exit 0). The binary otherwise dispatches on SUBCOMMANDS (`analyze`, `cross`, `endpoint`, `manifest`, `diff`, `facts`, `graph`, `analyze-envelope`, `validate-envelope`, `validate-rule-pack`, `init`, `contract`, `explain`, `version`, `help` — see main.rs's USAGE constant (it stays there on purpose — the MCP package's surface_prose meta-test reads that literal by path; cli/help.rs holds only the per-subcommand elaboration table)), not flags. This list is the whitelist CHECK A validates every `--flag`-shaped token in shipped messages against (union with `externalToolFlags`).
_docs.embedderFields: engine request-surface field names (crates/facade/src/lib.rs's AnalyzeRequest) that legitimately appear in a zzop message as 'the embedder dialect' — i.e. the field name a HOST APPLICATION embedding the engine (`zzop-facade`) directly (not through a config file) would set. Every native rule's disable-hint already says this explicitly: 'Disable via config `rules: {...}` (embedders: `disabledRules`)' — the hint's spelling flipped to the camelCase wire form on 2026-08-02 (`zzop_core::finding::disable_hint`), because the snake_case form is the Rust struct field name only and a JSON request spelling it is silently dropped. Kept to exactly the fields a message in the scanned dirs actually references today (see the rule_contracts meta-test's CHECK B doc comment for the verification) — extend only when a new message legitimately needs to name another embedder field, not preemptively.
_docs.embedderFieldShapes: One-line JSON shape per embedderFields entry, so an embedder field named in a zzop message is discoverable from this file alone (a consumer holding only the binary + this resource would otherwise see a bare name with no shape). Documentation only — no code path consumes this section (crates/config/src/mapper/warnings.rs reads configKeys via the CONFIG_SURFACE_JSON const; the rule_contracts meta-test reads the flat lists); keep its key set mirroring embedderFields exactly.
_docs.externalToolFlags: Flags of OTHER tools (never zzop's own) that a zzop message legitimately mentions when explaining an OUTSIDE cause for a symptom. Today that's exactly git's own `--depth` (a shallow clone, e.g. `git clone --depth=1`) and `--unshallow` (`git fetch --unshallow`, the fix) — both from crates/metrics/src/diagnostics.rs's thin-git-history warning. Kept minimal: enumerated by scanning the real tree, not pre-populated with every flag a tool happens to have.
_docs.allowlistedTokens: Literal tokens that are not config paths/keys at all but legitimately sit inside CHECK B's +/-120-char 'near the word config' window anyway — a filename convention (`zzop.config.jsonc`, the CLI's own config file, referenced as plain prose text today but allowlisted preemptively so a future backtick-quoted mention doesn't spuriously fail) or an unrelated identifier/header name that happens to share a sentence with a config-disable hint. Each entry's source is documented in the rule_contracts meta-test's CHECK B doc comment, not just here. `ir.io` — packages/mcp/src/tools/definitions.rs's analyze_repo/cross_repo descriptions name it as the raw-io OUTPUT field their own shaped MCP reply omits (the same co-location pattern as `crossLayer.unresolvedConsumes`: an output field, not an input config knob, mentioned near a config-honoring clause in the same sentence). `crossLayer.unconsumedProvides` joined 2026-08-01 for the same reason: S14 (`framework_silence/python_mount_prefix.rs`) tells the reader that the provides matching its wrongly-keyed consumes are sitting in that very bucket, one sentence away from the `trees[].topology.mountedAt` remedy it prescribes — naming the bucket is the point of the sentence, and it is a reply field rather than a knob.
_docs.mcpToolTokens: The zzop-mcp host's tool-surface vocabulary: every tools/call ARGUMENT name (packages/mcp/src/tools/definitions.rs inputSchema properties, enumerated by reading that file) plus the reply fields its self-description text backticks (`config`, `configWarnings`, `ruleOverridesApplied`, `distinctBucketKeyFirstSites`, `ir`). A DIFFERENT dialect from config-file keys — vouched as its own section (not allowlist noise) since the tool-surface files joined the reference-validation scan set (2026-07-17, when they still lived in the since-deleted host crate; they are packages/mcp/src today, still inside the scanned set), so a tool description naming a nonexistent argument fails CHECK B the same way a bad config key does. `ir` was added when analyze_repo/cross_repo's descriptions started naming the raw engine field their shaped MCP reply deliberately omits (see this file's `allowlistedTokens` doc for the paired `ir.io` entry — the dotted form is checked as an allowlisted token, not through this list, since CHECK B's dotted-token branch does not consult mcpToolTokens). `packsLoaded` was added when `validate_rule_pack`'s description started pointing authors at it (2026-07-17): the tool validates one pack's shape in isolation, so a pack `id` collision with a bundled/other pack — which replaces the loser WHOLE — is invisible to it and only surfaces at load time via the engine's `packsLoaded` report (plus its shadow warning), which the description now names by backtick. `warnings` was added (2026-08-09) when check_file's and check_endpoint's descriptions started naming the host-layer channels they stamp: their `Returns:` lists were closed lists that omitted `config`/`warnings`/`configWarnings`, which reads as a denial rather than silence — a model handed a `lexical-only` verdict had no reason to look at the one field that says WHY the parse degraded. Its two siblings were already vouched here; it was missing only because no description had backticked it yet. `architecture` and `gitWindow` were added (2026-07-17, git-signal disclosure-asymmetry fix batch) when analyze_repo's description started naming its own new reply field (`architecture`: a compact, capped `{pain, topRecommendation, criticalTop}` summary of the facade's `health`/`recommendations`/`critical` output, present only when git signals ran) and the forwarded engine echo field `gitWindow` ({recentDays, since}).
_docs.treeFields: Per-field type/requiredness for `configKeys.tree` (one entry of a `trees[]` array), read from crates/config/src/mapper.rs + crates/config/src/mapper/validation.rs (the config front end's own fail-fast gates): `root` — string, REQUIRED, non-empty; a path resolved against `base_dir` (see the path-resolution _docs paragraph below). `sourceId` — string, OPTIONAL; when omitted, defaults to the tree's OWN raw `root` string exactly as written (e.g. a tree with `root: "./api"` and no `sourceId` gets `sourceId: "./api"` — NOT the resolved absolute path and NOT just the root's basename). That is the CONFIG-file dialect default (this `trees[]`/`roots` mapping); a config-less/bare-path analyze request (no config file, no `trees[]` in play at all — e.g. an embedder calling `zzop-facade`'s analyze directly with a bare `root`) instead defaults an empty/missing `sourceId` to the analyzed root DIRECTORY's own basename, applied at the facade chokepoint every host funnels through (`apply_source_id_default`, `crates/facade/src/analyze.rs`, D14 2026-07-17) — lossy `to_str` fallback: the given root string verbatim if the basename can't be decoded (e.g. a bare drive root). `overlays` — string[], OPTIONAL; each entry is a path to a Mode B adapter envelope JSON file, resolved against THIS TREE'S OWN root (never `base_dir`, never the config file's directory — see `configKeys`'s own overlay-resolution note); an unreadable or non-JSON overlay is skipped with a warning, never a hard error. `mountedAt` — string, OPTIONAL; a whole-tree gateway/ingress prefix shorthand, validated to start with `/`, contain no `://` scheme, no `{}` placeholder, and no whitespace (a violation is a load-time `ConfigError`, not a warning). `clientBase` — string, OPTIONAL; the CALLING side's mirror of `mountedAt` — the path prefix this tree's own outbound http calls carry, for the case where the base is assigned from a cross-file constant (`axios.defaults.baseURL = settings.baseApiUrl`) and the never-guess extractor therefore reads nothing, leaving the calls keyed `GET /articles` while the provider serves `GET /api/articles`. Same validation as `mountedAt` (leading `/`, no `://` scheme, no `{}` placeholder, no whitespace; a violation is a load-time `ConfigError`). Applied to every keyed RELATIVE `http` consume of the tree, unscoped by client (a declaration is a statement about the whole tree, exactly as `mountedAt` is on the serving side); an unresolved consume and an absolute-URL key are never touched. Unlike `mountedAt`, stacking is warned rather than silent: if the code ALREADY carried a readable literal base, the declaration still applies (the declaration wins) but a `configWarnings`-adjacent analysis warning names both prefixes, because on the calling side a second prefix is usually a duplicate rather than a second real layer. A declaration that rewrites nothing also warns. `mounts` — array of `{ dir, at }` objects, OPTIONAL; `dir` must be tree-relative (must NOT start with `/`) and use forward slashes only (no backslash); `at` follows the same validation as `mountedAt`. `hosts` — string[], OPTIONAL; each entry a BARE host (no `://` scheme, no `/` path separator, no whitespace) — a full URL is rejected. `routes` — array of `{ key, role? }` objects, OPTIONAL; the lightweight route-fact injection channel for a route zzop could not resolve from source (a non-literal path, a dynamic verb, a computed URL): `key` is a required non-empty `"METHOD PATH"` string (e.g. `"GET /api/users"`, normalized through the same `http_interface_key` the extractors use so casing/trailing-slash don't matter), `role` is optional and exactly `"provide"` (default — the route is SERVED here) or `"consume"` (the route is CALLED from here). The facade expands the whole array into ONE synthetic adapter overlay of http provides/consumes (`crates/facade/src/config.rs`'s `routes_overlay`), so it composes through the identical cross-layer join path as a hand-authored `overlays` envelope; a `key` that is not a METHOD+PATH pair is soft-skipped with a warning at that layer (not a load-time `ConfigError`). Separately, `trees` itself (the array's own top-level key, sibling to `roots`) accepts the literal string `"auto"` instead of an array: this expands to one tree per workspace package (`sourceId` = each package's name), detected from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `package.json`'s `workspaces` field (crates/config/src/workspaces.rs) — a monorepo shortcut that turns the cross-layer join on with no hand-authored `trees[]` array. `roots` vs `trees: "auto"`: `trees: "auto"` always scans the CONFIG FILE'S OWN directory for workspace members; `roots` never steers auto mode (it has zero effect once `trees: "auto"` is in play). A config carrying BOTH is a conflict, not a silent merge — auto wins, `roots` is dropped, and the config gets one `configWarnings` entry naming that `roots` was ignored (`crates/config/src/workspaces.rs`'s `expand_auto_trees`).

embedderFieldShapes.adapterOverlays: NormalizedEnvelope[] — mode-B io overlays (partial envelopes, typically io + fragment channels for a few files) merged on top of native analysis for the tree; an invalid overlay is skipped with a warning
embedderFieldShapes.disabledRules: string[] of rule ids — those rules never run/report
embedderFieldShapes.packsDir: string | string[] — DSL rule-pack directory path(s), loaded in order (a later same-id pack replaces the earlier one whole); explicit null opts out of every DSL pack, bundled included. Config-file dialect: `packs.extraDirs` — `packsDir` is the embedder request field, not a valid zzop.config.jsonc key.
embedderFieldShapes.packsOnly: string[] of DSL pack ids — the opt-IN half of the pack axis: when non-empty, a pack whose id is absent does not run, so a caller wanting one subject area names it instead of enumerating the other eleven. EMPTY MEANS NO ALLOWLIST (every loaded pack runs), never allow-nothing. Scoped to PACKS only — native analyses (dead-candidates, scores, ...) carry bare ids in the same space but are not packs, so they keep running and stay disabledRules' business. Composes with disabledRules rather than overriding it (the allowlist selects, disabledRules still subtracts). Config-file dialect: `packs.only`.
embedderFieldShapes.profileRules: boolean — turns rule TIMING instrumentation on for this run (EngineConfig::profile_rules, the ESLint TIMING=1 equivalent), populating the output's `ruleTimings`. CLI dialect: the `--profile-rules` flag on `analyze`/`analyze-envelope`/`cross` (the envelope lane's pack evaluation feeds the same timing accumulator, so Mode A profiles too). Deliberately has NO zzop.config.jsonc key: a config file declares what is true about the PROJECT and gets committed, while a timing report is a question about ONE INVOCATION on one machine. Never changes findings/ir.
embedderFieldShapes.suppressions: { rule, path?, glob? }[] — drops findings for one rule (path = substring match, glob = full-path anchored; glob wins when both are set)
